parts.label: (a)
parts.text: State what is meant by the de Broglie wavelength.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Calculate the de Broglie wavelength of an electron moving at a speed of 4.9 × 10⁷ m s⁻¹.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text: State one similarity and one difference between an electron and a positron.

parts.label: (d)(i)
parts.lead: An electron moving at a speed of 4.9 × 10⁷ m s⁻¹ collides with a positron that is travelling at the same speed in the opposite direction. As a result of the collision, two gamma-ray photons are produced.
parts.text: State the name of this type of reaction.

parts.label: (d)(ii)
parts.text: State what happens to the electron and to the positron.

parts.label: (d)(iii)
parts.text: Explain why two gamma-ray photons are produced, rather than just one.

parts.label: (d)(iv)
parts.text: Show that the kinetic energy of the electron before the collision is 1.1 × 10⁻¹⁵ J.

parts.label: (d)(v)
parts.text: Use the information in (d)(iv) to determine, to three significant figures, the wavelength associated with the gamma radiation emitted in the collision.
